registry_size.source: data/products.json entry count, confirmed live at design time

concurrency.note: No --concurrency flag exists in this repo today (registry loop in commands_supervision.py:732 is a plain sequential `for entry in entries`). This model computes the concurrency=2 wall time the requirement asks for as a projection over the existing sequential per-repo cost, not a measurement of an existing parallel runner.

empty_shell_repositories.definition_caveat: "empty-shell" is not an existing term or lifecycle status in this codebase (verified: no match for empty_shell/empty-shell anywhere in src/). This model treats it as repositories that terminate before reaching AGENT_REVIEWING -- e.g. unonboarded entries with no ecosystem/policy_profile (loop.py:265-272, blocked before any clone or LLM call) or a FACTS_COLLECTING-stage block (BLOCKED_FACT_CONFLICT/BLOCKED_MISSING_EVIDENCE) -- both already exclude Qwen review calls today without any new code.
empty_shell_repositories.estimated_fraction_of_registry: unknown -- not measured in this design pass; the model below reports both a 0%-skip and a 20%-skip scenario so downstream planning isn't anchored to an invented number

lifecycle_stages_relevant_to_qwen.resume_mechanism: src/readme_agent/supervisor/loop.py:317-363 (supervise_repo) reads prior_full_state.readme_poc_lifecycle.status from StateBackend and resumes from that stage rather than restarting; product_truth_recovery.py:250-258 states the pipeline explicitly reprocesses "from durable state's actual position instead of crashing the whole repository." A repo whose last failure was, e.g., a merged-review transport failure resumes directly at AGENT_REVIEWING on the next pass -- it does not re-run FACTS_COLLECTING or CANDIDATE_GENERATED.

per_call_latency_inputs.model_choice: use the measured 1.6-6.1s range for the typical case and the 90s hard timeout as the worst-case single-call bound (a call that hits the timeout is itself a transport_failure trigger for this design's recovery path, not an unbounded wait)

single_facet_recovery.qwen_calls: up to 3 (1 merged + up to 2 recovery)

assumptions: Sequential per-repo review cost dominated by Qwen call latency (typical case, not the 90s timeout ceiling -- timeouts are the exceptional path this design exists to bound, not the common case).
concurrency=2 halves total wall time versus fully sequential, modulo the usual non-linear scheduling overhead which this model ignores as out of scope for a design task.

Only the AGENT_REVIEWING stage's Qwen calls are modeled here; clone/facts-collection/publish stage time is out of scope (see plans/investigations/evidence/verification-latency-root-cause-2026-08-19/root-cause-and-durable-design.md for the full end-to-end 10-25 minute portfolio-pass figures, which are NOT Qwen-call-specific).

pessimistic_case_20pct_need_recovery.note: ~7 repos need up to-3-call single-facet recovery, ~26 need 1 call

scenario_20pct_empty_shell_skip.note: 6 repos never reach AGENT_REVIEWING -- zero Qwen calls, zero wall-time contribution to this model; their cost lives entirely in FACTS_COLLECTING/onboarding, out of scope here

resumed_run_after_partial_failure.description: A run interrupted mid-registry (e.g. by a transient Docker-unavailable failure in a different repo's FACTS_COLLECTING stage, per plans/master.md's 2026-08-20 Stage-5-calibration changelog entry) resumes at each repo's own persisted lifecycle stage. Repos already past AGENT_REVIEWING contribute zero additional Qwen calls on resume; only repos still at or before AGENT_REVIEWING re-enter this cost model.

wall_time_estimate_33_repos_concurrency_.headline_estimate: With realistic recovery incidence and no empty-shell skipping, the full 33-repository registry's Qwen-review-call wall time at concurrency=2 is on the order of 1-2 minutes in the typical case, with a hard worst-case ceiling of 33 x 450s / 2 = ~4.1 hours if every single repo hit the full 5-call/90s-timeout worst case simultaneously -- a bound this design's recovery dispatcher exists specifically to keep the system away from, not an expected outcome.

caveats: No empty-shell fraction is measured anywhere in this repo today; both 0% and 20% scenarios are reported rather than asserting a single number.
No concurrency=2 runner exists to benchmark directly; this is a projection, explicitly labeled as such.

The 'headline estimate' worst-case (4.1h) assumes maximally-correlated failure across all 33 repos, which is not realistic for independent gateway calls -- included only to bound the design's own worst-case ceiling, not as a planning number.
